opening ceremony Part of [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics")
[![Image 4](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG/330px-2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG)

_Fire and Nature_ segment of the opening ceremony
[![Image 5: Map](https://maps.wikimedia.org/img/osm-intl,10,-33.847222222222,151.06333333333,270x200.png?lang=en&domain=en.wikipedia.org&title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&revid=1378179363&groups=_a133fbdba3dd5caa9a311ab39d9e894eafd0d84d&parser=parsoid)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Map/10/-33.847222222222/151.06333333333/en)
Date 15 September 2000;26 years ago(2000-09-15)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-GuardianReview-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SOCOG9AugPressRelease-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-tvguide-3)
Time 19:00 – 23:19 [AEDT](link_2) ([UTC+11](link_3))[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-tvguide-3)
Venue[Stadium Australia](link_4)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-GuardianReview-1)
Location*   [Sydney](link_5), [New South Wales](link_6), [Australia](link_7)
*   [33°50′50″S 151°03′48″E / 33.84722°S 151.06333°E / -33.84722; 151.06333](link_1)
Filmed by Sydney Olympic Broadcasting Organisation (SOBO)
Participants 12,500
Footage[Sydney 2000 Opening Ceremony – Full Length](link_8) on [YouTube](link_9)

The [opening ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games_ceremony#Opening "Olympic Games ceremony") of the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") took place on the evening of Friday, 15 September 2000 in [Stadium Australia](link_4), [Sydney](link_5), during which the Games were formally opened by then-[Governor-General](link_10)[Sir William Deane](link_11).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-GuardianReview-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-tvguide-3)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SOCOG9AugPressRelease-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:4-4) As mandated by the [Olympic Charter](link_12), the proceedings combined the formal and ceremonial opening of this international sporting event, including welcoming speeches, hoisting of the flags and the parade of athletes, with an artistic spectacle to showcase the host nation's culture and history.

Veteran ceremonies director [Ric Birch](link_13) was the director of ceremonies[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:0-5) while [David Atkins](link_14) was the Artistic Director and Producer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-6) Its artistic section highlighted several aspects of Australian culture and history, showing Australia's flora and fauna, technology, multiculturalism, and the hopeful moment of reconciliation towards [Aboriginal Australians](link_15).[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:0-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:1-7) The ceremony had a cast of 12,687 performers,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:2-8) seen by a stadium audience of around 110,000.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:1-7)

The ceremony began at 19:00 [AEDT](link_2) and lasted over four-and-a-half hours.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:1-7) Around 3.7 billion viewers worldwide watched the ceremony on TV.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:4-4)

The ceremony was described by the [President of the International Olympic Committee](link_16) (IOC) [Juan Antonio Samaranch](link_17) as the most beautiful ceremony the world had ever seen.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:0-5)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:5-9) Consistent with normal major production management, the music was pre-recorded under studio conditions to ensure its quality.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-smh_prerecord-10)

The stadium's French-language announcer was Pascale Ledeur, while the English-language announcer was Australian actor [John Stanton](link_18). Ledeur was also the French announcer at the opening ceremonies of the [Atlanta 1996](link_19) and [Salt Lake City 2002](link_20) Olympic Games.

The **2000 Summer Olympics torch relay** was the transferral of the [Olympic Flame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Flame "Olympic Flame") to [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"), that built up to the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics"). The torch travelled to various island nations as part of a tour of [Oceania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania "Oceania") before beginning an extensive journey around Australia. For the first time the Flame was taken underwater, with a special flare-like torch taken on a dive down to the [Great Barrier Reef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Barrier_Reef "Great Barrier Reef"). At the opening ceremony the cauldron was lit by [Aboriginal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_Australians "Indigenous Australians") athlete [Cathy Freeman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cathy_Freeman "Cathy Freeman").

## Torch

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Torch")]

The design of the torch reflected three famed areas of Australian culture: the [boomerang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boomerang "Boomerang"), the [Sydney Opera House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Opera_House "Sydney Opera House"), and the waters of the [Pacific Ocean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean"). The concept also reflected the elements of earth, fire, and water.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-OfficialReport-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-eweek-2) This was achieved across three layers of the torch. The first, inner layer contains the fuel system and combustor, the second contains the fuel canister, and the outer layer is a specially textured aluminium shell. A combination of copper, brass, aluminium, and stainless steel was used in its construction, and the fuel comprised 65 percent butane and 35 percent propane. In total, 14,000 torches were produced.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-eweek-2) The distance covered by each torchbearer was 105.478 km.

## Torchbearers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Torchbearers")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Torch_bearer.jpg/250px-Torch_bearer.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Torch_bearer.jpg)

Fred Atkins taking the Torch through [Taree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taree "Taree"), New South Wales

A total of 13,400 torch-bearers were involved in the relay. The Greek leg of the route saw 800 people carry the torch, while 1,500 people were involved across [Oceania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania "Oceania"). As part of the vast traversal of Australia, 11,000 people carried the torch within the country.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-3)[Anna Booth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anna_Booth "Anna Booth") was the Australian who chaired the 2000 Summer Olympics torch relay committee and she brought the torch to Australian soil on 8 June.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-4)

The first Australian torch-bearer was Sophie Gosper in May, the daughter of International Olympic Committee (IOC) Vice-President [Kevan Gosper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevan_Gosper "Kevan Gosper"). Her selection caused considerable controversy with accusations of corruption directed at the [Hellenic Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellenic_Olympic_Committee "Hellenic Olympic Committee") (HOC). Greek-Australian Yianna Souleles was originally due to receive the torch in Olympia but she was replaced at late notice by Gosper. Kevan Gosper accepted the invitation for his daughter to carry the torch while claiming to be unaware that this would make her the first Australian to have the honour.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-ISOR-5)

The HOC's invitation was seen as an attempt to carry favour with the IOC after being warned that its delays put the planned 2004 Olympics (scheduled to be held in Greece) in jeopardy.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-6) Gosper's acceptance of the invitation was portrayed by the media as being [nepotistic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nepotism "Nepotism") and inappropriate, with Australian politicians, Olympic athletes, and officials from various Olympic Committees condemning the move. Gosper initially defended his actions but would go on to make a public apology, claiming that fatherly pride had clouded his judgement. He gave up his role in the relay at the [Melbourne Cricket Ground](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne_Cricket_Ground "Melbourne Cricket Ground") despite having previously described it as "the most important moment of my life since I won a silver medal [there]".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-ISOR-5)

## Route

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Route")]

The Flame was lit during a ceremony in Olympia, as has been tradition at all the Summer Games since [those in 1936](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1936_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay "1936 Summer Olympics torch relay"). The Flame is initiated by using a parabolic mirror that concentrates the sun's rays. However, due to some cloud cover on the day of the ceremony, there was insufficient sunlight to create the required level of heat. A backup, lit on the previous day during rehearsals, was used instead. The remainder of the ceremony could then take place.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_torch_relay#cite_note-OfficialReport-1)

The relay always begins in Greece and travels from Olympia to [Athens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athens "Athens") and the [Panathenaic Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panathenaic_Stadium "Panathenaic Stadium"). Derartu Tulu in 2019

**Derartu Tulu**[NL](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laureate)[COL](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel) ([Oromo](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oromo_language): _Daraartuu Tulluu_, [Amharic](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amharic): ደራርቱ ቱሉ; born 21 March 1972) is an Ethiopian former [long-distance runner](https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long-distance_runner), who competed in track, [cross country running](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Cross_country_running "Cross country running"), and road running up to the [marathon](https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Marathons "Marathons") distance.

## Quotes

[[edit](https://en.wikiquote.org/w/index.php?title=Derartu_Tulu&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Quotes")]

*   "It was a hobby my dad I shared - he also loved riding,"
*   "It was a beautiful childhood. When I went to school, when I looked after our cattle, I literally used to ride a horse wherever I went."
*   "I followed her until 400m was left - and I suddenly sped up and took the lead,"
*   "We became friends and she's the woman I admire most."
*   "After I won gold in Barcelona, many women runners started thinking that it is possible to win big competitions,"
*   "Our results have gone down very much. Our neighbour and main rival Kenya has taken over on every international competition. We have to take lessons from those competitions, we have to look deep into Ethiopian athletics and identify what went wrong and bring our glorious days back." 
    *   [Africa Olympic stories: Derartu Tulu, the first black African woman to win gold,](https://www.bbc.com/sport/africa/53467530)25 July 2020,by **Emeline****Nsingi-Nkosi-BBC Africa Sport**

*   “For everything, you had to run,”
*   “The market was far away from our village, so we'd run all the way. To get water, you had to run. To pick up wood, you had to run.”
*   "The moment created a friendship, an emotional moment, and a significant message to the world.”
*   “I’ve watched the video many times down the years, not the race itself, but the 26th lap. It makes me emotional and speechless every time." 
    *   [Derartu Tulu: How Ethiopia’s Olympic champion united a continent and inspired a generation with her running,](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/ethiopia-derartu-tulu-united-africa-inspired-generation-running)29 March 2024,By Evelyn Watta

*   “I feel very emotional being back, it was a moment that changed my life forever,”
*   “It was an extraordinary journey to get to the Olympics in 1992. So just to be able to walk out to the stadium and represent my country was amazing."
*   “Looking back, it wasn't the 25 laps of the race that mattered, but it was the 26th which made an impact.”
*   “It was a very happy moment for both of us. Even if I can’t speak English, we could feel each other's emotion and I could see Elana smiling,”
*   “It should also be remembered that Elana is not only popular in South Africa now, but also in Ethiopia because of Barcelona 1992. It creates a very good vibe of peace and unity.”
*   “I wasn’t planning on being president but I was the chosen one! People proposed me as the candidate and I was elected,”
*   “Sport taught me how to give back to others, and share what you have for their improvement. It paved the way to a better life and gave me great lessons in leadership for when I became the president.”
*   "Every person who participates in sport can learn those values, make friendships, and bridge differences. That’s the real power of sport.”
*   “I’m still passionate and busy in the world of sport and about the impact it can have on people’s lives. I feel that it is my purpose in life, to use sport to impact people in a positive way,” 
    *   [Reunited: Derartu Tulu and Elana Meyer remember iconic 'lap 26' at Barcelona 1992 Olympics](https://www.olympics.com/en/news/derartu-tulu-elana-meyer-reunited-barcelona-1992-olympic-values),27 September 2022,By Andrew Binner

# Noémie wins Fox family battle as Jess’s hopes of golden Olympic treble end

This article is more than 2 years old

*   Australia’s Olympic flagbearer comes last in kayak cross heat
*   Noémie wins to progress to semi-final on Monday at Paris Games
*   [Latest medal table](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/ng-interactive/2024/aug/04/paris-olympics-2024-medal-table-latest) | [Live Paris schedule](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/ng-interactive/2024/jul/29/paris-olympics-2024-live-schedule-dates-times-updated) | [Full results](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/ng-interactive/2024/jul/19/paris-olympics-2024-results)

[Jack Snape](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/jack-snape) in Paris

Sun 4 Aug 2024 12.05 EDT First published on Sun 4 Aug 2024 11.48 EDT

Share

[2 2](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/article/2024/aug/05/paris-olympics-noemi-jess-fox-kayak-cross-quarter-final-heat#comments)

[Prefer the Guardian on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=theguardian.com)

Jess Fox’s golden run at Paris has come to end, after she couldn’t recover from a tangle at the start of her kayak cross heat from which her sister Noémie deftly emerged to claim victory.

The result is a sudden end to the 30-year-old’s hopes of a third gold medal in France, the country of her birth, at the Games where she is Australia’s flag bearer.

“That’s kayak cross, and you can have a plan, but nothing goes to plan. I’m gutted, but at the same time, when you see your little sister win the heat, I was really proud of her,” Jess said.

[![Image 3: Gold Medalists Mollie O’Callaghan, Lani Pallister, Brianna Throssell and Ariarne Titmus of Australia pose after winning the women's 4x200m freestyle relay at Paris 2024](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/1e9c4d5ea643715f1eabccbc25464c6df95669e8/0_172_5387_3232/master/5387.jpg?width=460&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=155bf8957926a6d1beab114c116e7dc7) Australia enjoys its best start to an Olympics as women lead gold rush in Paris Read more](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/article/2024/aug/04/paris-olympics-2024-australia-medal-record-gold-rush-women-swimming-kaylee-mckeown)

“Its really tough, but there’s also some relief in finishing, there’s partly disappointment to not progress today, and to not try and have a crack at that third medal progress, but there’s pride, relief and exhaustion from the last week of competing.”

The younger Fox took an early lead in the four-woman race and stayed in front throughout the combative dash down the course.

“It was sad to see her not get up to second behind me”, Noémie told Channel Nine. “I would have loved to [progress to] the quarter-finals together, but that’s the sport. It’s so brutal, and it’s really every man for themselves, essentially. So yeah, I cheered her on in the gold medal runs, and hopefully she cheers me on until the end too.”

The elder Fox got caught up in a duel with Martina Wegman in the early stages , and had to work hard to make up ground on Spain’s Maialen Chourraut in second place for much of the 200m race.

“I just didn’t pull out my best race,” she said. “It was tough off the start. I got really tangled, and I was trying to chase.”

She finally caught the Spaniard on the final upstream gate, but couldn’t get past her and ultimately finished fourth, ending her hopes of a third gold medal in Paris.

Noémie started in the right lane alongside Jess, and said it can be difficult for those on the inside who get caught in the early scramble.

“The start is probably the most important thing to try get out in front and to really punch through,” she said. “I’d say the two far right lanes are definitely the fastest lanes, and it kind of depends who’s next to you as well. But I like that there’s a bit of less contact from the start, so I’m not sandwiched from the get go.”

She expressed her regret she couldn’t continue with her sibling. “We were hoping to meet in the finals, but yeah, it was an incredible race, a really tough lineup again in the heats, and I know the quarter-finals will just be as stacked.”

Noémie will feature in the quarter-finals, and potentially the semi-finals and final, on Monday. Australians Tristan Carter and Tim Anderson are also through to the quarter-finals in the men’s event.

At the same time, Trump is using the FCC – which is supposed to be an independent regulator in the public interest – to settle political scores: The FCC targeted ABC after Jimmy Kimmel made a joke about the First Lady, and Trump suggested that the agency should punish the host of Meet the Press for making a factual statement the president disliked.

# Inside the dirtiest race in Olympic history: ‘It wasn’t fair. I wasn’t on a level playing field’

This article is more than 1 year old

How did the women’s 1500m in the 2012 London Olympics get its unenviable reputation? Athletes who were cheated out of medals talk about what happened that day – and how the results have slowly unravelled

![Image 3: Esther Addley](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/uploads/2023/06/05/Esther_Addley.png?width=75&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)

[Esther Addley](https://www.theguardian.com/profile/estheraddley)

Sat 26 Apr 2025 07.00 EDT Last modified on Wed 31 Dec 2025 05.08 EST

Share

[Prefer the Guardian on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=theguardian.com)

T he tunnel in which athletes wait before they enter a stadium ahead of a major race is “by no means a friendly place to be”, says [Lisa Dobriskey](https://www.teamgb.com/athlete/lisa-dobriskey/8croDwMaGKrmt3NocABk8) – and as a former Team GB athlete who won Commonwealth gold and world championship silver at 1500m, she has stood in enough of them to know. “Different people handle it differently,” she says. “Some people are really relaxed and friendly; other people just look right through you. It’s scary. I remember my coach saying to me, ‘When you go to the Olympics, you’ll be standing next to the meanest, toughest, hardest people that you’ll ever face.’ Everybody wants to win.”

As it turned out, the wait to walk into London’s Olympic stadium for the final of her event in August 2012 was even more stressful than she’d been warned. With British excitement at fever pitch, support and expectation for home athletes had reached near hysteria at times. “It was terrifying,” Dobriskey says of hearing the 80,000-strong crowd in the stadium. “People were yelling, people were screaming, it was overwhelming.”

Having come an [agonising fourth](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HMnnptAtSas) in Beijing four years earlier, Dobriskey had battled her way into the London final after a [nightmarish year](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/18703586). In early 2012 she developed a stress fracture of her thigh, delaying her track training for months; then in late May, a niggling problem with her breathing led to her being rushed to hospital with a life-threatening pulmonary embolism. Doctors advised her not to think about running for six months. Instead, less than three months later, here she was in an Olympic final, having [won her heat](https://youtu.be/GGbFJdWlI3M?si=XJVHOZ6XPijAtzrZ&t=533) and with commentators talking up her chances of a medal.

“That weight, that pressure,” she says, “I took it all on personally.” [Footage of the race buildup](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lWzqfiWRE9Q) shows the 13 athletes lining up jumpily on the track, with Dobriskey on the far outside lane. Her name is announced first, to a roar from the crowd. She bounces on her toes, then stands nervously, her eyes closed, breathing deeply.

![Image 4: Gold Medalist Asli Cakir Alptekin of Turkey (R) and teammate and Silver Medalist Gamze Bulut celebrate after the Women’s 1500M Final at the London 2012 Summer Olympics on August 10, 2012 in Stratford, London](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/53e0341552bda673a441957fbb6bc075175d66e8/0_119_3500_2202/master/3500.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/apr/26/dirtiest-race-in-olympic-history-womens-1500m-london-2012#img-2)

In the final lap, Turkish team-mates Asli Cakir Alptekin ​and Gamze Bulut surged ahead to take gold and silver … Photograph: Brian Kersey/UPI/Shutterstock

![Image 5: The women’s 1500m race at the London 2012 Olympics](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/7c80cff6aff2a53776fa6795fc635e1f556cde55/0_0_5184_3145/master/5184.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/apr/26/dirtiest-race-in-olympic-history-womens-1500m-london-2012#img-3)

… leaving Maryam Yusuf Jamal, seen here in the lead, to finish third. In 2021, that bronze was upgraded to gold. Photograph: Tim Clayton/Corbis/Getty Images

A little more than four minutes and 10 seconds later, it was all over. Asli Cakir Alptekin, a Turkish athlete who had won the European championships title a month earlier, had again taken gold after leading from the front for the last 300m. Silver was claimed by another Turkish competitor, Gamze Bulut, after a surge to the line as several others faded. Bronze went to Bahrain’s Maryam Yusuf Jamal. Dobriskey, who had been near the rear of the field and unable to fight her way back, crossed the line in 10th place, almost three seconds off the pace.

She was bitterly disappointed, even embarrassed, at the result – but also deeply frustrated. A month earlier, after competing at[a Diamond League meet in Paris](https://www.runnerspace.com/eprofile.php?event_id=1021&do=videos&video_id=73376) at which a Moroccan athlete, Mariem Alaoui Selsouli, and Çakir Alptekin had raced seemingly effortlessly to a fast time, Dobriskey had privately contacted the world athletics governing body, the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF, since renamed World Athletics), to say she believed the athletes were doping. Sure enough, days later [Selsouli had tested positive](https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/18985217) for a banned diuretic – which [can be used](https://www.sportintegrity.gov.au/news/integrity-blog/2024-05/furosemide-use-sport) to flush other performance-enhancing substances out of the body – and been barred from competing at London 2012.

![Image 6: (L-R) Lisa Dobriskey of Great Britain and Laura Weightman of Great Britain look on after competing in the Women’s 1500m Final on Day 14 of the London 2012 Olympic Games at Olympic Stadium on August 10, 2012 in London, England](https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/578e3234c13c63f139ef800bd670abe9bc8e1a94/0_89_2105_2585/master/2105.jpg?width=120&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none)[View image in fullscreen](https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/apr/26/dirtiest-race-in-olympic-history-womens-1500m-london-2012#img-4)

Lisa Dobriskey and Laura Weightman of Great Britain after the race. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

So when, moments after the London final, [BBC Five Live’s Sonja McLaughlan asked](https://youtu.be/1MWjYGxRQTA?si=FDYy050TfFrHqJJR&t=13445)how “comfortable” Dobriskey felt that Cakir Alptekin, the new Olympic champion, had previously served a two-year drugs ban, she told the truth. “I’m very uncomfortable with that,” she said. “I’m probably going to get in trouble for saying so, but I don’t believe I’m competing on a level playing field.” The then relatively new [athlete biological passport scheme](https://www.wada-ama.org/en/athlete-biological-passport#:~:text=WADA's%20Athlete%20Biological%20Passport%20Operating,the%20detection%20of%20blood%20doping.) During the **Parade of Nations** portion of the [2000 Summer Olympics opening ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony "2000 Summer Olympics opening ceremony"), athletes from each country participating in the Olympics paraded in the arena, preceded by their flag. The flag was borne by a sportsperson from that country chosen either by the [National Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Olympic_Committee "National Olympic Committee") or by the athletes themselves to represent their country.

## Parade order

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_Parade_of_Nations&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Parade order")]

As the nation of the [first](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Summer_Olympics "1896 Summer Olympics") modern [Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games "Olympic Games"), [Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greece "Greece") entered the stadium first; whereas, the host nation of [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_at_the_2000_Summer_Olympics "Australia at the 2000 Summer Olympics") marched last. Other countries entered in alphabetical order in the language of the host country ([English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language")), according with tradition and [IOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") guidelines.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_Parade_of_Nations#cite_note-1)

Whilst most countries entered under their [short names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_sovereign_states "List of sovereign states"), a few entered under more formal or alternative names, mostly due to political and naming disputes. [Macedonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Macedonia "North Macedonia") entered as "**F**ormer Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia'" because of the [naming dispute with Greece](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macedonia_naming_dispute "Macedonia naming dispute"). The [Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan") (commonly known as Taiwan) entered with the compromised [name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Taipei "Chinese Taipei") and [flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Taipei_Olympic_flag "Chinese Taipei Olympic flag") of "Chinese **T**aipei" under T so that they did not enter together with [conflicting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two_Chinas "Two Chinas")[People's Republic of China](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Republic_of_China "People's Republic of China") (commonly known as China), which entered as the "People's Republic of **C**hina" under C. The [Republic of the Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_the_Congo "Republic of the Congo") entered as just "**C**ongo" while the [Democratic Republic of Congo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Republic_of_Congo "Democratic Republic of Congo") entered with its full name. [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"), [Micronesia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federated_States_of_Micronesia "Federated States of Micronesia"), [Moldova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Moldova "Republic of Moldova"), [Laos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laos "Laos"), [Brunei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brunei "Brunei") and the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") all entered under their formal names, respectively "Islamic Republic of **I**ran", "Federated States of **M**icronesia", "Republic of **M**oldova", "**L**ao People's Democratic Republic", "**B**runei Darussalam" and "**U**nited States of America".

A record of 199 nations entered the stadium with the exception of [Afghanistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Emirate_of_Afghanistan_(1996%E2%80%932001) "Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (1996–2001)"), a nation banned by the [IOC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") in 1999 because of the extremist rule of the [Taliban](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban "Taliban")'s oppression on women and its sports.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_Parade_of_Nations#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_Parade_of_Nations#cite_note-3) The parade of nations also featured a unified entrance by the athletes of the North and South Korea, holding a specially designed [unification flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unification_flag "Unification flag") bearing the name "Korea": a white background flag with a blue map of the Korean peninsula; however, the two teams competed separately.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_Parade_of_Nations#cite_note-4) Four athletes from [East Timor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Timor "East Timor") marched directly in the opening ceremonies as _[individual Olympic athletes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Individual\_Olympic\_athletes\_at\_the\_2000\_Summer\_Olympics "Individual Olympic athletes at the 2000 Summer Olympics")_ before the host nation. Without the existence of the National Olympic Committee, they were allowed to compete under the [Olympic flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_flag "Olympic flag").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_Parade_of_Nations#cite_note-5)

The [opening ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Games_ceremony#Opening "Olympic Games ceremony") of the [2000 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics "2000 Summer Olympics") took place on the evening of Friday, 15 September 2000 in [Stadium Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadium_Australia "Stadium Australia"), [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"), during which the Games were formally opened by then-[Governor-General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_Australia "Governor-General of Australia")[Sir William Deane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Deane "William Deane").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-GuardianReview-1)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-tvguide-3)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SOCOG9AugPressRelease-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:4-4) As mandated by the [Olympic Charter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Charter "Olympic Charter"), the proceedings combined the formal and ceremonial opening of this international sporting event, including welcoming speeches, hoisting of the flags and the parade of athletes, with an artistic spectacle to showcase the host nation's culture and history.

Veteran ceremonies director [Ric Birch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ric_Birch "Ric Birch") was the director of ceremonies[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:0-5) while [David Atkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Atkins "David Atkins") was the Artistic Director and Producer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-6) Its artistic section highlighted several aspects of Australian culture and history, showing Australia's flora and fauna, technology, multiculturalism, and the hopeful moment of reconciliation towards [Aboriginal Australians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_Australians "Aboriginal Australians").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:0-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:1-7) The ceremony had a cast of 12,687 performers,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:2-8) seen by a stadium audience of around 110,000.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:1-7)

The ceremony began at 19:00 [AEDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Australia "Time in Australia") and lasted over four-and-a-half hours.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:1-7) Around 3.7 billion viewers worldwide watched the ceremony on TV.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:4-4)

The ceremony was described by the [President of the International Olympic Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_International_Olympic_Committee "President of the International Olympic Committee") (IOC) [Juan Antonio Samaranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Antonio_Samaranch "Juan Antonio Samaranch") as the most beautiful ceremony the world had ever seen.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:0-5)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:5-9) Consistent with normal major production management, the music was pre-recorded under studio conditions to ensure its quality.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-smh_prerecord-10)

The stadium's French-language announcer was Pascale Ledeur, while the English-language announcer was Australian actor [John Stanton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Stanton_(actor) "John Stanton (actor)"). Ledeur was also the French announcer at the opening ceremonies of the [Atlanta 1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") and [Salt Lake City 2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_Winter_Olympics "2002 Winter Olympics") Olympic Games.

## Preparations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Preparations")]

As one of the motto's of the games was the "Games of the New Millennium", there was a major reevaluation on how to present the Olympics, which included the ceremonies.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:0-5) In regards to the protocol of the ceremony, there had been incremental changes in the ceremonies format after [1960 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_Summer_Olympics "1960 Summer Olympics") where the Olympic Anthem was readopted, and with the symbolic release of doves starting at [1994 Winter Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_Winter_Olympics "1994 Winter Olympics").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-protocolbureau-11) For Sydney, the ceremonies producers chose to have the lighting of the cauldron at the end of the ceremony, rather than having it in the middle of the protocol section in previous ceremonies.

The artistic section, where it showed the host countries culture through a separate presentation, gained more prominence since [Moscow 1980](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony "1980 Summer Olympics opening ceremony"). The Moscow Opening ceremony was one that Australian director [Ric Birch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ric_Birch "Ric Birch") had been personally impressed by.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch200410-12) This was the first opening ceremony which showed the host country's national culture through one narrative rather than multiple segments[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Vox-13)

By 2000, Birch had worked on global events for over 18 years producing high-profile events. He directed the [1982 Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1982_Commonwealth_Games "1982 Commonwealth Games") opening and closing ceremonies, and the cultural and the opening ceremonies for [World Expo 88](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Expo_88 "World Expo 88"), both held in [Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane"). He was also asked to direct and produce some segments for the 1984 and 1992 Summer Olympic opening and closing ceremonies and was involved in Sydney's handover segment at the [1996 Summer Olympics closing ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics_closing_ceremony "1996 Summer Olympics closing ceremony"). Birch was hired to produce the ceremonies in September 1993.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch2004209-14) The idea for the cauldron reveal at the end of the ceremony was planned during the design process of [Stadium Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stadium_Australia "Stadium Australia"), as they needed to consider requirements of the water structure of the northern stand and extra supports for the height of the cauldron arc.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWest200059-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Stephens-16) For the rest of the ceremony, Birch wanted a model where each segment was organised by a specialty director, and was given free artistic reign in their segment as long as it was telling its part of the story.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch2004239-17) The team of directors were assembled in 1997, with David Atkins as the head Artistic Director and Producer.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch2004248-18) In August 2000, the organisers announced the eleven main performers, the twenty-one composers and four conductors held in a press conference in Melbourne.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SOCOG9AugPressRelease-2)

Ahead of the opening of the games, and as testing beds for the content of the ceremonies, the [Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics#Organisation "2000 Summer Olympics") developed four [Olympic Arts Festivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics#Sydney_Olympic_Arts_Festival "2000 Summer Olympics") beginning in 1997. The first festival, the _[Festival of the Dreaming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Festival\_of\_the\_Dreaming "Festival of the Dreaming")_ was established by [Rhoda Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhoda_Roberts "Rhoda Roberts"). The festival was a celebration of [Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aboriginal_and_Torres_Strait_Islander "Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander") arts and culture.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-20) Roberts was later selected as a segment director for the ceremony. The second festival was _A Sea Change_, in which artists and companies from Australia and [Oceania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania "Oceania") explored "the influence of the sea on Australian life as a means to explore the changing political and cultural climates in Australia".[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-ciddor2001-21) The third festival, "Reaching the World", took the form of an international tour, showcasing Australian culture.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-ciddor2001-21) The final festival, the Sydney 2000 Olympics Arts Festival, ran before and during the Olympics, and served as a showcase for the diversity and depth of the arts in Australia.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-ciddor2001-21)

## Proceedings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Proceedings")]

### Prelude

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Prelude")]

As spectators arrived, they found on their seats a yellow [Globite case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Briefcase "Briefcase") with Olympic stickers on the front, reminiscent of those that once prevailed in Australian schoolrooms in the 20th century. Inside the case were a pair of green and gold socks, cheer band, a replica of the 2000 Summer Olympics torch, lapel pin, event program, postcard, cards, earplugs, stickers and a Kodak [CD-ROM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CD-ROM "CD-ROM"). The torch and cheer band – set with movement-sensitive lights – illuminated the darkened stands during the Fire segment, Arrivals segment and the lighting of the cauldron, while [Australian Olympic Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_at_the_Olympics "Australia at the Olympics") socks appeared prominently on the sea of waving hands during Australia's entry to the stadium.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-MAAS-29)

The Prelude segment lasted an hour before the ceremony started. It was hosted by [Seven Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven_Network "Seven Network")'s Sports Commentator David Fordham and news presenter [Chris Bath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Bath "Chris Bath"), while seven months pregnant with her first child, live on the northern stage in the stadium. It featured various performances, including a [Welcome to Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welcome_to_Country "Welcome to Country") from the [Wangal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wangal "Wangal") people, children singing the official Team Welcome Song "G'day G'day", a recognition of the Bidding team and the Olympic volunteers, a recognition from the [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") of the [Olympic Truce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Truce "Olympic Truce"), [Mexican waves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wave_(audience) "Wave (audience)"), and a singalong of "[Waltzing Matilda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waltzing_Matilda "Waltzing Matilda")" with [John Williamson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Williamson_(singer) "John Williamson (singer)").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWest200017-30)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Preludesegments-23)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-CNNBrian-31)

### Welcome and Anthem

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Welcome and Anthem")]

"Advance Australia Fair"  
(Opening Ceremony)

> **Verse 1 (Sung by Human Nature as A cappella)**  
>  Australians all let us rejoice,  
>  For we are young and free;  
>  We've golden soil and wealth for toil;  
>  Our home is girt by sea;  
>  Our land abounds in nature's gifts  
>  Of beauty rich and rare;  
>  In history's page, let every stage  
>  Advance Australia Fair.  
>  In joyful strains then let us sing,  
>  Advance Australia Fair.  
>   
> **Verse 2 (Sung by Julie Anthony with orchestra)**  
>  Beneath our radiant Southern Cross  
>  We'll toil with hearts and hands;  
>  To make this Commonwealth of ours  
>  Renowned of all the lands;  
>  For those who've come across the seas  
>  We've boundless plains to share;  
>  With courage let us all combine  
>  To Advance Australia Fair.  
>  In joyful strains then let us sing,  
>  Advance Australia Fair.  
>   
> **Verse 1 Reprise (all voices)**

The ceremony began with a countdown composed by Richard Mills performed by [Sydney Symphony Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Symphony_Orchestra "Sydney Symphony Orchestra"). The large screens counted down from 60 to 1. Starting at 23, footage from previous games appeared on the screens ending with art by Sydney artist [Ken Done](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Done "Ken Done") that read "Opening Ceremony".

The arrival of a lone rider [Steve Jefferys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Jefferys "Steve Jefferys"), dressed in a drizabone and akubra hat, with his Australian Stock Horse _Ammo_, galloped into the empty stadium floor reared in the middle of the stadium. Jefferys then cracked his [stockwhip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whip "Whip"), and 120 riders and their Stock Horses entered the stadium performing a "[Musical ride](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_ride?action=edit&redlink=1 "Musical ride (page does not exist)") " to an arrangement of the main theme of the 1982 film _[The Man from Snowy River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Man\_from\_Snowy\_River\_(1982\_film) "The Man from Snowy River (1982 film)")_, composed by [Bruce Rowland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Rowland_(composer) "Bruce Rowland (composer)").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Fitzsimons-32) Each rider held a flag with the [Olympic Rings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Rings "Olympic Rings") coloured blue. One of the configurations formed the five Olympic Rings. This was a tribute to the heritage of the [Australian Stock Horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Stock_Horse "Australian Stock Horse"). Many of its riders were from [Scone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scone,_New_South_Wales "Scone, New South Wales").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-33)

A giant banner painted by Sydney artist Ken Done was unfurled, depicting the [Sydney Harbour Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Harbour_Bridge "Sydney Harbour Bridge") in bright colours, saying "G'Day" to the world.

The [governor-general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_Australia "Governor-General of Australia")[Sir William Deane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Deane "William Deane"), the [prime minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Australia "Prime Minister of Australia")[John Howard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Howard "John Howard"), and the president of the IOC [Juan Antonio Samaranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Antonio_Samaranch "Juan Antonio Samaranch"), arrived after a jazz fanfare was performed by [James Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Morrison_(jazz_musician) "James Morrison (jazz musician)") and Swing City, [his brother's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Morrison_(drummer) "John Morrison (drummer)") Big Band.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Ferin-34) The Australian National Anthem, _[Advance Australia Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advance\_Australia\_Fair "Advance Australia Fair")_, was then sung by both [Human Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_Nature_(band) "Human Nature (band)") and [Julie Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julie_Anthony_(singer) "Julie Anthony (singer)"), accompanied by the [Sydney Symphony Orchestra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Symphony_Orchestra "Sydney Symphony Orchestra") under the baton of [Simone Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simone_Young "Simone Young").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-35) The Stock Horse riders still on the field then swapped their Olympic flags for [Australian flags](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Australia "Flag of Australia") before riding out of the stadium.

#### Deep Sea Dreaming

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Deep Sea Dreaming")]

The Hero Girl, [Nikki Webster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Webster "Nikki Webster") arrived in beachwear and basked in the light on a beach.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-37) She falls asleep on the beach and drift off into a dream. The performers represented the sea and the various aquatic fauna appear and move around the arena floor. The Hero Girl was then hoisted up in the air by overhead wires and swam with the sea creatures.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38) Other swimmers were also present, being coached (on a large screen) by Australian swimming coach [Laurie Lawrence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurie_Lawrence "Laurie Lawrence"). This was a tribute to the [Great Barrier Reef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Barrier_Reef "Great Barrier Reef") off the coast of Australia.

#### Awakening

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Awakening")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Wandjina_at_mt_elizabeth.jpg/250px-Wandjina_at_mt_elizabeth.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wandjina_at_mt_elizabeth.jpg)

The Awakening segment featured a 32-metres-long cloth showing a Wandjina spirit – a large head that shows the eyes and nose, but with no mouth.

The Awakening segment celebrated Australia's [Aboriginal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_Australians "Indigenous Australians") and [Torres Strait Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torres_Strait_Islander "Torres Strait Islander") cultures, the world's oldest continuous living culture, dating back at least 60,000 years. A [Yolngu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yolngu "Yolngu") elder and songman, Djakapurra Munyarryun,[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-ABC_News_Online-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Djakapurra_Munyarryun-40) guided the girl through the [songlines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songline "Songline") of connections to the land and the protocols for welcoming others to indigenous land. The segment featured Indigenous Australians from the Central Desert, the Numbulwar, Yirrkala, Ramingining and Manningrida peoples of Arnhem Land, Torres Strait Islanders, and the Koorie clan of NSW.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-ABC_News_Online-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Djakapurra_Munyarryun-40) The segment ended when the [Wandjina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wandjina "Wandjina") ancestral spirit appears[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-41) (in the form of a 32-metre-long cloth in the style of a [rock art portrait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_Australian_art#Stone_art "Indigenous Australian art")) roaring and flinging a lightning bolt to ignite a bushfire.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEWest200025%E2%80%9327-42)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38)

#### Fire & Nature

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Fire & Nature")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8e/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG/250px-2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_1.JPEG)

The Nature segment

The Fire and Nature segment showcased the [Australian outback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_outback "Australian outback"), and its unique wildlife and flora. It began with various fire performers (jugglers, breathers) moving across the stadium field, symbolising the advance of a [series of bushfires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bushfires_in_Australia "Bushfires in Australia").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38) In the aftermath, performers representing the flora stir as the land is replenished with all types of life. The stadium field is now filled with performers dressed in costumes representing various flowers including Australia's distinctive wild flowers such as the [Golden Wattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Wattle "Golden Wattle") (Australia's national flower), the [Waratah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waratah "Waratah") (State flower of New South Wales), the [Sturt's Desert Pea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sturt's_Desert_Pea "Sturt's Desert Pea"), [Water Lilies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_Lilies "Water Lilies") and [Eucalypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eucalypt "Eucalypt") flowers.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38) The fauna, which were represented by seven large paintings by [Ngemba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ngiyampaa "Ngiyampaa") artist [Jeffrey Sammuels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Sammuels?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jeffrey Sammuels (page does not exist)") and were then revealed, depicting the Indigenous animal life in Australia.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch2004262-43) The flowers once more were illuminated before moving out of the stadium.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38)

#### Tin Symphony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Tin Symphony")]

In the Tin Symphony segment presents the start and consequences of the British settlement in Australia.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38) The segment began with the arrival of Captain [James Cook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Cook "James Cook"), with naturalist [Joseph Banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Banks "Joseph Banks") and crew, with bicycles to represent his ship, [HM Bark _Endeavour_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HM_Bark_Endeavour "HM Bark Endeavour"), during Captain Cook's exploration of the Australian east coast. A [rabbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbits_in_Australia "Rabbits in Australia") inside a cage was one detail found aboard the ship.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBirch2004265-44) Captain Cook lit a firework to mark the start of the segment.

**Tin Symphony Part 1** — The music, co-written and co-produced by [Ian Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Cooper_(violinist) "Ian Cooper (violinist)") and John Frohlich, includes an Irish jig montaged with drums, bush sounds and voice.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-45) A number of performers dress as the iconic Australian [bushranger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bushranger "Bushranger")[Ned Kelly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ned_Kelly "Ned Kelly") (with costumes based on Sir [Sidney Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Nolan "Sidney Nolan")'s series of Ned Kelly paintings) then appear onto the stadium floor, with while other performers bring out other symbolic items of rural settler life such as [corrugated iron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrugated_iron "Corrugated iron") and [storm water tanks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Storm_water_tank "Storm water tank") present. A mechanical horse like vehicle was present which then changed into a [wind mill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wind_mill "Wind mill"). Australian rural culture such as woodcutting and whip cracking were showcased. Irish dancers present in this section danced on the corrugated iron sheets, with umbrellas made up to look like giant cogs and wheels to represent the industrial growth of Australia.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38)

**Tin Symphony Part 2** — The tempo changes as Australia's suburban aspects were introduced. In the middle of the stadium floor, a shed was constructed from the corrugated iron sheets. Out of the shed comes a unique representation of sheep, an important livestock for Australia. The sheep were represented by performers in cardboard boxes, that move along with the music. Australian [suburbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suburbia "Suburbia") was represented as the performers emerged from the cardboard boxes with [Victa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victa "Victa")[lawn mowers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawn_mowers "Lawn mowers") to form the Olympics Rings.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38) The giant mechanical horse then made another appearance, before the hero girl gave an apple to it. At the end of the segment, the mechanical horse neighed to signify the conclusion.

#### Arrivals and Under Southern Skies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Arrivals and Under Southern Skies")]

The Arrivals segment of the ceremony celebrated Australia's [multiculturalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiculturalism "Multiculturalism") and its migrant culture formed by the [Australian Gold Rushes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Gold_Rushes "Australian Gold Rushes") and the aftermath of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") for Australia, with a float, soundtrack and [costumes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costumes "Costumes") symbolising each [continent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Continent "Continent") the migrants came from, coloured by the five Olympic rings that represent each continent.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38) First, performers as migrants from [African](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ethnic_groups_of_Africa "List of ethnic groups of Africa") danced into the stadium wearing [black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black "Black") costumes with African beat music. They were followed by dancers in [yellow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow "Yellow") and Asian style musical elements, symbolising the arrival of [Asian migrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_people "Asian people"), led by two pairs of yellow Chinese Lion dancers. [European migrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethnic_groups_in_Europe "Ethnic groups in Europe") were introduced by the colour [green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green "Green") with electronic music, further adding to the growing party on the stadium field. The music changed again into American style music and a splash of [red](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red "Red"), both symbolising the arrival of migrants from the [Americas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americas "Americas"), was introduced into the stadium. Finally, performers representing migrants from [Oceania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceania "Oceania") with an emphasis on [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand") and [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander "Pacific Islander") communities came into the stadium in vivid [blue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue "Blue") costumes. The five floats maneuvered into position to represent their respective coloured rings of the Olympic flag. By the crescendo of the segment, four of the floats (Asia, America, Europe and the Oceanian) surround the African float as the performers from all the represented continents merged into one big group and them rushed out from the middle to form the [Australian continent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia_(continent) "Australia (continent)").

The performers stood with arms out reached towards the audience, forming the coastline of Australia and thus symbolising Australia's welcoming arms to people from all over the world. Then many children dressed in the Olympic colours flooded into the arena and formed a solid shape of Australia, as the performers from the sequence before left the performance floor. Webster then performed the song _Under Southern Skies_ with five people representing each continent standing with her, as the children formed a large representation of the Southern Cross constellation with their lanterns.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38)

#### Eternity

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Eternity")]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Sydney_Olympics_Opening_Ceremony.jpg/250px-Sydney_Olympics_Opening_Ceremony.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sydney_Olympics_Opening_Ceremony.jpg)

The Eternity segment showed thousands of tap dancers.

The next segment began with [Adam Garcia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adam_Garcia "Adam Garcia") standing on the central float in the middle of the stadium field. He began his performance by [tap dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tap_dance "Tap dance") and inviting more performers onto the stadium. More dancers filed onto the stands where the audience was sitting who also joined in with performance. Several cherry picker cranes in the centre with the floats began to slowly rise up with the crescendo of the music. The dancers symbolised the workers building a new Australia for the future. The dancers in the stands rushed out onto the stadium floor to join their fellow dancers. Some of the dancers held square sheets of steel that they both danced on and held in their hands to reflect light out as they danced. By the finale of this segment, large steel frames rose from each float to form a tall structure. In the middle were the hero girl and the Aboriginal elder, who looked wondrously out into the audience, surveying the workers.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-SMH-Secrets-38) Then as the close of the presentation approached, the performers from the other segments all came out and joined in with those already dancing. A large representation of the [Sydney Harbour Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney_Harbour_Bridge "Sydney Harbour Bridge") composed of sparklers was set off in the middle of the stadium with the word "[Eternity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eternity_(graffito) "Eternity (graffito)")" shown in the middle of the bridge.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-:5-9)

This segment was inspired by the then popular theatrical show Tap Dogs, and the soon to be released movie, _[Bootmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bootmen "Bootmen")_. Peewee Ferris's remix of the music was played as the performers slowly moved their way out of the stadium into the crowd.

### Sydney 2000 Olympic Band

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Sydney 2000 Olympic Band")]

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9c/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_3.JPEG/250px-2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_3.JPEG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony_3.JPEG)

The Olympic Band performs

A massed marching band of 2,000 musicians performed a melody of Australian and international classics, and previous Olympic themes. It included "[Also Sprach Zarathustra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Also_Sprach_Zarathustra "Also Sprach Zarathustra")", "[Chariots of Fire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chariots_of_Fire_(instrumental) "Chariots of Fire (instrumental)")", "[Ode to Joy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphony_No._9_(Beethoven)#IV._Finale "Symphony No. 9 (Beethoven)")", "[Bugler's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bugler's_Dream "Bugler's Dream")", "[Waltzing Matilda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waltzing_Matilda "Waltzing Matilda")", and [John Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Williams "John Williams") "Olympic Fanfare & Theme". The band consisted of 1,000 Australian musicians, with the remaining 1,000 musicians being from other countries around the world.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-ABC_AM_BAND-46) There were trumpets, trombones, mellophones, baritones, sousaphones, flutes, piccolos, clarinets, alto, tenor, and baritone saxophones, snares, basses, multitenors, cymbals, and glockenspiels. The massed band was so large that six [conductors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conductor_(music) "Conductor (music)") were required for the segment. The band members wore [Driza-Bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Driza-Bone "Driza-Bone") riding coats which had been especially modified for the band members.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-48) The band was one of the few live sound performances at the night.

Marching and wind bands have made regular appearances in Summer Olympic Ceremonies throughout the 20th Century. However, this segment was controversial in the lead up in the local media, as when it was announced in 1999, three-quarters of the band were from overseas while also ignoring Sydney based wind bands.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-NYT-Band-49) The organisers had to renegotiate the number of international performer invitations for this segment so that half the band was made up of Australian performers on the night. Birch always envisioned the band to be both larger than anyone had seen at an Olympic ceremony, and for an international band to welcome international athletes.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-ABC_AM_BAND-46) Reviews immediately after the ceremony stated that the band was so "skilled and entertaining in their fashion" that "it was hard to believe that their part was ever in doubt."[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Fitzsimons-32)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Seven_ImmediateReview-50) In contrast, [Peter FitzSimons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_FitzSimons "Peter FitzSimons") opined that the band was a non-sequitur compared to the rest of the [Australiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australiana "Australiana") pageantry, and was seen as an element of [cocacolanisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocacolonization "Cocacolonization") by some in Australia.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#cite_note-Fitzsimons-32) Since 2000, marching and wind bands have not seen a major appearance at an Olympics opening ceremony, except for the Hellenic Naval Band during the entrance of the Presidents in the [Athens ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony "2004 Summer Olympics opening ceremony") in 2004, an appearance from the [Grimethorpe Colliery Band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimethorpe_Colliery_Band "Grimethorpe Colliery Band") during the [Pandemonium segment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#Pandemonium_(21:09%E2%80%9321:25) "2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony") of the London ceremony in 2012 and the [Republican Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Guard_(France) "Republican Guard (France)") marching band showing up for the [Égalité segment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Summer_Olympics_opening_ceremony#%C3%89galit%C3%A9 "2024 Summer Olympics opening ceremony") of the Paris ceremony in 2024.
